dimensions.assessment: Changes the technological and operational framework for federal environmental reviews and permits, aiming to increase efficiency and transparency.
dimensions.evidence: taking a standardized, digital-first perspective to environmental reviews and authorizations at Federal agencies... will improve document quality

summary: The ePermit Act requires the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and federal agencies to digitize, standardize, and modernize environmental reviews and authorizations under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. It establishes data standards, prototype tools, minimum functional requirements, and a unified interagency data system that includes a shared cloud-based authorization portal for project sponsors, federal agencies, and the public.

affected_groups.effect: Must implement new data standards and minimum functional requirements, submit progress reports, and adopt unified interagency data systems and tools for environmental reviews.
Can use a unified, secure portal to submit documentation, track application and review timelines, and collaborate digitally with federal agencies.
Gains access to a portal providing non-sensitive data on project types, timelines, environmental reviews, mitigation measures, and public comment opportunities.
Receives direct access to aggregated performance data, analytics, implementation reports, and artificial intelligence support systems for real-time oversight.

key_provisions: CEQ must develop and update data standards and comprehensive data categories for environmental reviews within 60 days of enactment.
CEQ must design, test, and build prototype tools to assist agencies with case management, application portals, public comment tracking, and automated workflows.
CEQ must publish implementation guidance for federal agencies regarding data standards and minimum functional requirements within 120 days of enactment.
Federal agencies must compare existing systems, submit implementation plans, and begin implementing data standards and minimum functional requirements within specified timelines.
CEQ and federal agencies must develop a unified interagency data system by December 1, 2027, featuring a common cloud-based authorization portal hosted by the General Services Administration.
CEQ must oversee a shared services pilot, including the authorization portal, within one year of enactment.
missing_information: The total authorized funding amount or specific budgetary appropriations needed to build and maintain the unified interagency data system and authorization portal.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The ePermit Act requires the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and federal agencies to digitize, standardize, and modernize environmental reviews and authorizations under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. It establishes data standards, prototype tools, minimum functional requirements, and a unified interagency data system that includes a shared cloud-based authorization portal for project sponsors, federal agencies, and the public.
summary_detail.significance: This bill directs a government-wide digital transformation of federal environmental reviews and permitting processes, creating unified software systems, shared data standards, and a central cloud portal across all relevant federal agencies.
